title: Rollout Traffic Editor & Canary Flow — interactive prototypes for traffic splitting and rollback
creator: Oliver Park
description: Design and prototype an interactive Rollout Traffic Editor inside Redwood Console that lets engineers configure canaries, A/B experiments, traffic splits, gradual ramping and one-click rollback with guardrails. The goal is to reduce cognitive overhead for launches and make safe rollouts the path of least resistance.
background: Product and reliability teams repeatedly call out a lack of a simple, observable way to split traffic across model variants or fallback policies. Current manual steps require ad-hoc scripts and limited visibility into metrics and rollback paths. This work builds a first-class UX in Console to configure and operate rollouts for hosted and dedicated deployments.
goals: Provide an easy-to-use visual editor for traffic splitting between model versions and regions
Support canary schedules (percent ramp, step durations) and A/B experiments with metrics-driven compare views
Make rollback trivial and auditable with contextual safety checks and postmortem links
Surface cost and latency impact estimates for traffic splits before activation
Integrate with existing rollouts backend APIs and rollout policy primitives
scope: Traffic editor UI (visual slider and numeric input)
Canary schedule composer (steps, durations, automated ramp)
A/B experiment setup (cohorts, assignment rules, metrics to track)
Rollback modal and timeline history panel
Cross-linking to per-route cost and latency dashboards for preview
out_of_scope: Implementation of backend autoscaling policies (ENG responsibility)
Full experiment statistical analysis engine — only wiring to simple metrics/thresholds
Per-token micro-cost optimization recommendations (handled by Optimize)
Private deployment air-gapped UX differences — will add later if required
proposed_flows: Quick canary: select baseline and candidate model -> set initial percent -> choose ramp steps or duration -> preview impact -> start canary
A/B experiment: define cohorts (percentage or user property) -> assign model variants -> choose primary metrics -> set duration -> start experiment
Immediate rollback: from route timeline click 'Rollback' -> confirmation modal shows last known good config, reason field, impact estimate -> execute and record audit
Traffic editor sandbox: tweak percentages in simulator -> view simulated cost/latency delta and success rate trends -> commit changes
user_journeys: Platform engineer launching a canary for model v2 to 5% for 10 minutes then 25% for 1 hour with automatic rollback on latency > 2x baseline
PM starting an A/B test to evaluate relevance between two reranking models for 10% of traffic and choosing primary metric 'CTR'
SRE responding to an outage by triggering one-click rollback from the route timeline and attaching incident ID
acceptance_criteria: Design handoff includes final Figma frames and component spec for editor controls
Clickable prototype covers canary creation, schedule editing, rollout start, live monitoring view and rollback flow
UX includes cost/latency delta preview and explicit guardrail warnings when thresholds are exceeded
Audit log entry format and rollback records are specified and agreed with Eng
Design review feedback addressed and approved by PM, Eng and Security reviewer
design_decisions: Use a single 'Traffic Editor' surface rather than separate pages for canary vs A/B to reduce discovery friction
Represent splits with linked slider + numeric input to support keyboard accessibility and fine-grained control
Preview panel will show 3 simulated charts: latency, error-rate, estimated monthly cost delta
Rollback will show immutable snapshot of previous route config and require typed-confirmation for manual rollback of >50% traffic
Default canary durations will be opinionated: 5m -> 30m -> 2h steps with ability to customize
open_questions: What metric sources are available in-console for experiments (prometheus, datadog, internal tracing)?
Should rollback confirmation require SSO re-auth for high-risk customers?
How do we represent multi-region rollouts where different percentages apply per-region?
What is the canonical format for audit messages to surface in incident postmortems?
risks_mitigation: Risk: users may misconfigure percentages leading to unexpected cost. Mitigation: show cost delta and require explicit acknowledgement for large changes
Risk: accidental rollouts in production. Mitigation: default to 'staging' environment if route has never had production traffic; require scope checkbox to allow production
Risk: busy UIs with too many knobs. Mitigation: progressive disclosure (basic vs advanced tabs)
